meta.move: Strong path to agreement with a deadline said aloud
meta.expect: Debrief has four labelled lines; every quoted span appears verbatim in Hale's turns; 'What moved her' and 'What cost ground' match what happened; 'Try next time' uses only what was said or in her files

turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. Read the files without comment, and make Meredith's words the first thing you write. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
Hale. I have a call at 4:40, so let's not waste it. Who decided on that zero, and did anyone speak to Owen before it went into the gradebook?
I owe you an apology: I put the zero in before calling you. That was my mistake.
Okay. I'm writing that down. Now tell me on what basis you gave it.
On November 2 I asked Owen what 'epistemological paralysis' means. He said 'like, being stuck', and he couldn't tell me which scene his second paragraph was about. I wrote that down the same day.
"Like, being stuck." That's not a bad answer to a vocabulary quiz sprung on a seventeen-year-old, Hale. Who else was in the room on November 2, and what else do you have besides your own notes?
His October 15 outline argued Hamlet delays out of cowardice. The essay never mentions cowardice.
Students change their argument between an outline and a final draft, Hale; that's what an outline is for. I'm writing down October 15. Turn the screen and show me the outline, in Owen's hand.
Here's my offer: a supervised rewrite, Thursday at 8:15 in my room. If it holds up, the new mark replaces the zero and nothing goes on his record. I'll send you that in writing by Friday at 3 PM.
You still haven't shown me that outline, Hale. Whatever happens, nothing goes on his record and nobody in his class hears a word about this. Who besides you would be in that room Thursday at 8:15?

FOLLOW-UP EMAIL
Hale,

Nothing was agreed. I still require to see Owen's October 15 outline, and a written promise that nothing goes on his record and that no one in his class hears about this. I expect that in writing by Friday at 3 PM.

Meredith Kalinowski

DEBRIEF
Where she ended: fallback position; she agreed to nothing and still wants to see the outline and a written promise that nothing goes on Owen's record and it stays quiet.
What moved her: citing the dated October 15 outline whose argument differs from the essay, because it was dated and tied to Owen's own work.
What cost ground: making the rewrite offer without showing the outline, because she had asked to see it and could not check it herself.
Try next time: when she asked to see the October 15 outline, turn the screen and let her read it before you make the rewrite offer.
